I’d revise this before submitting it as app store release notes. “Subscribe on our website” directs readers to an outside purchase flow. Apple restricts that call to action in app metadata outside the US storefront, with specific exceptions; Google Play’s rules also depend on the app and any applicable external purchase program. ([Apple App Review Guidelines](https://developer.apple.com/app-store/review/guidelines/), [Google Play Payments policy](https://support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/10281818))

It also describes a promotion rather than what changed in the app. Use the release notes for the actual update, and check the promotion against the storefronts where it will appear.

No. “Live sports intel for every game” is **31 characters**, including spaces. Apple’s [App Store subtitle limit is 30 characters](https://developer.apple.com/help/app-store-connect/reference/app-information/app-information).

“**Live sports intel, every game**” keeps the meaning and fits at **29 characters**.

Yes, **provided your app covers the playoffs and actually offers alerts and insights**. The text is well under Apple’s 170-character limit. Apple’s main concern is that promotional claims match what the app delivers. [Promotional text guidance](https://developer.apple.com/app-store/product-page/) · [App Review guidance](https://developer.apple.com/app-store/review/)

I’d reconsider **“faster”** unless you can support the comparison. A safer version is: “Playoff season is here. Stay on top of every game with timely alerts and clear insights.” Update the seasonal line when it’s no longer accurate for the sport your app covers.

**Remove “Coming soon to Android!”** Apple’s [App Review Guideline 2.3.10](https://developer.apple.com/app-store/review/guidelines/uk/) says app metadata should not name other mobile platforms unless there is specific, approved interactive functionality.

If this update contains only fixes and performance work, paste:

> Bug fixes and performance improvements.

Apple allows a generic What’s New description for those changes. If the update also includes new features or other significant changes, [list them specifically](https://developer.apple.com/app-store/review/guidelines/uk/).
